# Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice

## Original exercise

James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
\(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).

> 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
> prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.

## Definitions and complete target

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

source_steps.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Use N001 and H002 to count |I|=n. By H005 choose an integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V; its cardinality is n since the e basis of N001 has n elements. Tensoring the integer coordinate isomorphism with R gives R-coordinates on M_R: finite sums ∑_{i∈I}r_i⊗m_i have unique coefficients r_i∈R. Explicitly the coordinate homomorphisms of M extend to these coordinates, and the sum map is their inverse. Under iota these basis tensors go to m_i, still complex-linearly independent, so iota is injective. This proves freeness of rank n and shows its image spans V over ℂ. Admissibility H005 gives preservation of M by every X_r,Y_r; extension by R gives preservation of M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve them; h=xy−yx by H003 preserves them too.

Fix i,j∈I. Evaluate using N001. X_λ kills e_k for k<λ and takes e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Therefore Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ. Also X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, so X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ. In Pi Y_(λ−j), an input e_k with kj goes past the end and is zero. At k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,j); hence Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Since λ

Compose the identities F002. On the e basis, E_iλ E_λj=E_ij; thus E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002. Consequently E_ij preserves M_R for all i,j. Together with F001 and F002 these are the asserted lattice and matrix-unit identities. This reasoning has used distinct complex weights only in N001 and makes no assertion about distinct weights modulo p.

By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. For any c∈J_j, the preserving map E_ij of N002 sends c e_j to c e_i, so c∈J_i. Interchanging i and j gives J_i=J_j. Thus all these R-submodules equal J=J_0.

For arbitrary u∈M_R, choose its coordinates d using the e basis N001: iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k. Applying E_ii and N002 gives d_i e_i∈iota(M_R), so d_i∈J_i=J by F001. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. Consequently the sum-of-coordinates map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear bijection, with inverse the coordinate projections, and M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k after the injective identification iota of N002.

By N002, M_R has n generators over R. The image of these generators under E_ii generates J e_i by F001. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise F002 would give M_R=0, whose complex span is zero, contrary to N002 and the nonempty basis of V in N001. Thus F001 and F002 give the full common-module and direct-sum assertions.

Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the images 1⊗c0 of a finite generating set of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. The multiplication map is given on pure tensors by ρ⊗c0↦ρc0∈ℂ, with ρ∈ℚ and c0∈J; it is well-defined by R-balancing. Since ℚ is the fraction field of R⊂ℚ (H001), a common nonzero denominator in R combines any finite tensor sum into d0^(-1)⊗c0 with 0≠d0∈R and c0∈J. The image of such an expression is c0/d0; a zero image implies c0=0 and hence a zero tensor. Thus multiplication is injective and identifies QJ with the rational span of J.

Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. N002 states that M_R is free of rank n, so M002 gives dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R M_R)=n. Tensoring the coordinate isomorphism of N003 gives ℚ⊗_R M_R≅∏_{i∈I}QJ: on a pure tensor with coordinates (gamma_i), the map sends ρ⊗(∑_{i∈I}gamma_i e_i) to (ρ⊗gamma_i)_{i∈I}; inverse maps insert the coordinates and sum. These inverse maps are balanced and linear, so this identification needs no flatness assumption. Apply M001 with A=ℚ, B=I and constant family C_i=QJ. Here I is finite with |I|=n by N001; QJ is a finite-dimensional vector space by F001, hence free and finitely generated. We obtain dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}QJ)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. Therefore n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, r=1.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonempty tuple g_1,…,g_k of nonzero generators of J, as permitted by N003. By F001 and F002, J lies in a one-dimensional rational line, and its nonzero vector a spans that line. Consequently each g_j=q_j a with a nonzero rational q_j. This proves the rational-coordinate description of a generating set; it is derived from the rank calculation rather than assumed merely from J⊂ℂ.

For each nonzero rational q_j, strip the factors p from its integer numerator and denominator. Since p is prime by H001, this gives q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j, with eta_j=ν_j∈ℤ and both numerator and denominator of u_j prime to p. Thus u_j and u_j^(-1) are in R. Put ν=min_j eta_j, which exists for the nonempty finite tuple of F003, and b=p^ν a≠0. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j−ν)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j−ν≥0. Conversely, for any generator attaining the minimum, multiplication of that generator by its unit u_j^(-1) gives b; hence b∈J and Rb⊆J. The first inclusion on generators gives J⊆Rb, so J=Rb.

N003 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}Rb e_i. Its coordinate sum map shows that (b e_i) spans over R; since b≠0 and the e family is complex-linearly independent by N001, it is R-linearly independent. Thus it is an R-basis. The same reasoning works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001 and F002 this proves the asserted rank and basis conclusions, exporting existence of such b without fixing its private identity.

By H001, every integer prime to p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. The formula defining kappa:R→K is independent of fractional representatives by cross multiplication, preserves addition and multiplication, and extends the integer map. The balanced tensor maps V_K=M⊗_ℤ K→M_R⊗_R K and back are m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c and (s⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗kappa(s)c. The tensor relations show that both are well-defined; the two composites fix pure tensors, hence are identity maps. Thus they are inverse K-linear isomorphisms. Since the maps act only on scalar factors, they intertwine every operator preserving M, including x,y,h,X_r,Y_r by N002.

The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. Its kernel is pR: a reduced fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator is divisible by p, and division of that numerator by p stays in R. Consequently R/pR≅F_p and M_R/pM_R is an F_p-module. The maps M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K and back send u⊗c to [u]⊗c and [u]⊗c to u⊗c. Changing u by a multiple of p changes u⊗c by zero, since p=0 in K. These formulas are balanced for the quotient R-action, are independent of representatives, and are inverse on pure tensors. They give the second K-linear isomorphism and commute with all induced lattice operators. Combine with F001 to obtain both tensor identifications asserted in the output.

Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb using N004. The family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R by N004, using iota from N002. Define beta_i to be its reduced image in V_K through F001. Scalar extension of its coordinate maps gives a K-basis: every pure tensor has its finite coordinate expansion in beta_i, and the extended coordinate maps take beta_i to the corresponding coordinate unit vectors, proving independence. Therefore dim_K V_K=|I|=n=λ+1>0 by N001 and H002. Applying N001 to b e_i and using the tensor isomorphisms gives x beta_0=0, x beta_i=(λ−i+1)beta_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<λ, y beta_λ=0; h beta_i=(λ−2i)beta_i. All coefficients are the integer images in K. This proves the required basis and its generator matrices.
For each r∈I, r≤λ

Choose the basis beta supplied by N005 and define T by its displayed formula. Let W⊆V_K be any K-linear subspace. Assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. Closure under x,y implies closure under their nonnegative powers. The divided-power indices in T_ij are λ−i,λ,λ−j, all within 0,…,λ; N005 identifies the corresponding X,Y with scalar multiples of those powers. A linear subspace is closed under scalar multiplication and compositions of preserving maps, so W is invariant under every T_ij.
In the zero case temporarily assume L2: W={0}. Then the desired disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately. Discharge L2 to obtain the implication for this case.

For the other case assume L3: W≠{0}. A nonzero subspace contains a nonzero vector, and the beta basis of N005 expands any such vector uniquely. Its coefficients cannot all be zero. Thus there exist a vector w∈W, a coefficient family c∈K^I and an index j∈I with w=∑_{k∈I}c_k beta_k, w≠0 and c_j≠0. Record this compatible joint existence before choosing the witnesses.

Choose compatible w,c,j as in F003. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit action of N005 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. By F001 this vector belongs to W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives beta_i∈W. This holds for every i; since beta is a K-basis, W=V_K. No chosen vector or coordinate is present in that conclusion. Discharge L3 to obtain: if W≠{0}, then W=V_K.

Classical case elimination on W={0} or W≠{0}, using F002 and F004, gives W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W: every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V_K. N005 also gives dim_K V_K=λ+1>0, so V_K is nonzero. By H003 and the definition of L_K, x,y,h span its lattice-induced action; invariance under those generators is equivalent to L_K-invariance. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. H001 and H002 give characteristic p and 0≤λ

Let A be a semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective linear map between finite free A-modules has source rank at most target rank), let B be a finite index type, and for each t∈B let C_t be an additive commutative monoid with an A-module structure, free and finitely generated over A. source_outputs.N001: n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v; for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V, and y^(λ+1)v=0 (hence all higher lowering powers vanish). On this basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For all i∈I and natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.
source_outputs.N002: iota embeds M_R as the R-span of M in V; M_R is free of rank n over R and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r (r≥0) preserves M and M_R, and x,y,h preserve M and M_R. For every i,j∈I, E_ij preserves M_R (under iota). The following identities hold on V: Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ, X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ, Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j), where binom(λ,j) is a unit in R.
source_outputs.N003: For every i∈I one has J_i=J. The R-module J⊂ℂ is nonzero and finitely generated. The map (c_i)_{i∈I}↦∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism ∏_{i∈I}J→iota(M_R), so, identifying M_R through iota, M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.
source_outputs.N004: The multiplication map ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ is injective and its image is the rational span of J, a one-dimensional ℚ-vector space. There exists b∈J with b≠0 and J=Rb. For any such b, the family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R identified with iota(M_R).
source_outputs.N005: The natural tensor maps give K-linear isomorphisms V_K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K, intertwining all lattice operators. There exists a K-basis (b_i)_{i∈I} of V_K obtained from an R-basis (b e_i) of M_R with b∈J nonzero. In particular dim_K(V_K)=n=λ+1>0. On this basis the induced operators satisfy xb_0=0, xb_i=(λ−i+1)b_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, yb_i=(i+1)b_(i+1) for i<λ, yb_λ=0, hb_i=(λ−2i)b_i, with integer coefficients interpreted in K. The reduced operators T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ−i)(Y_λ X_λ)Y_(λ−j), for i,j∈I, obey T_ij b_k=δ_jk b_i for every k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 for j=k and 0 otherwise.
source_outputs.P: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183:

The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V, and y^(λ+1)v=0 (hence all higher lowering powers vanish). On this basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For all i∈I and natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.
value.N002: iota embeds M_R as the R-span of M in V; M_R is free of rank n over R and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r (r≥0) preserves M and M_R, and x,y,h preserve M and M_R. For every i,j∈I, E_ij preserves M_R (under iota). The following identities hold on V: Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ, X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ, Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j), where binom(λ,j) is a unit in R.
value.N003: For every i∈I one has J_i=J. The R-module J⊂ℂ is nonzero and finitely generated. The map (c_i)_{i∈I}↦∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism ∏_{i∈I}J→iota(M_R), so, identifying M_R through iota, M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.
value.N004: The multiplication map ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ is injective and its image is the rational span of J, a one-dimensional ℚ-vector space. There exists b∈J with b≠0 and J=Rb. For any such b, the family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R identified with iota(M_R).
value.N005: The natural tensor maps give K-linear isomorphisms V_K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K, intertwining all lattice operators. There exists a K-basis (b_i)_{i∈I} of V_K obtained from an R-basis (b e_i) of M_R with b∈J nonzero. In particular dim_K(V_K)=n=λ+1>0. On this basis the induced operators satisfy xb_0=0, xb_i=(λ−i+1)b_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, yb_i=(i+1)b_(i+1) for i<λ, yb_λ=0, hb_i=(λ−2i)b_i, with integer coefficients interpreted in K. For every 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K and the induced divided powers X_r,Y_r equal (r!)^(-1)x^r,(r!)^(-1)y^r. Every binom(λ,j) for j∈I is nonzero in K. The reduced operators T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ−i)(Y_λ X_λ)Y_(λ−j), for i,j∈I, obey T_ij b_k=δ_jk b_i for every k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 for j=k and 0 otherwise.
value.P: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.

Let A be a semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective linear map between finite free A-modules has source rank at most target rank), let B be a finite index type, and for each t∈B let C_t be an additive commutative monoid with an A-module structure, free and finitely generated over A. Then finrank_A(∏_{t∈B} C_t)=∑_{t∈B} finrank_A(C_t). Here finrank is cardinal module rank converted to a natural number (zero if that cardinal is infinite).

10: public import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Subalgebra.Tower
11: 
12: /-!
13: 
14: # Localizations of domains as subalgebras of the fraction field.
15: 
16: Given a domain `A` with fraction field `K`, and a submonoid `S` of `A` which
17: does not contain zero, this file constructs the localization of `A` at `S`
18: as a subalgebra of the field `K` over `A`.
19: 
20: -/
21: 
22: @[expose] public section
23: 
24: 
25: namespace Localization
26: 
27: open nonZeroDivisors
28: 
29: variable {A : Type*} (K : Type*) [CommRing A] (S : Submonoid A) (hS : S ≤ A⁰)
30: 
31: section CommRing
32: 
33: variable [CommRing K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
34: 
35: theorem map_isUnit_of_le (hS : S ≤ A⁰) (s : S) : IsUnit (algebraMap A K s) := by
36:   apply IsLocalization.map_units K (⟨s.1, hS s.2⟩ : A⁰)
37: 
38: /-- The canonical map from a localization of `A` at `S` to the fraction ring
39:   of `A`, given that `S ≤ A⁰`. -/
40: noncomputable def mapToFractionRing (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization S B]
41:     (hS : S ≤ A⁰) : B →ₐ[A] K :=
42:   { IsLocalization.lift (map_isUnit_of_le K S hS) with commutes' := fun a => by simp }
43: 
44: @[simp]
45: theorem mapToFractionRing_apply {B : Type*} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization S B]
46:     (hS : S ≤ A⁰) (b : B) :
47:     mapToFractionRing K S B hS b = IsLocalization.lift (map_isUnit_of_le K S hS) b :=
48:   rfl
49: 
50: theorem mem_range_mapToFractionRing_iff (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization S B]
51:     (hS : S ≤ A⁰) (x : K) :
52:     x ∈ (mapToFractionRing K S B hS).range ↔
53:       ∃ (a s : A) (hs : s ∈ S), x = IsLocalization.mk' K a ⟨s, hS hs⟩ :=
54:   ⟨by
55:     rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
56:     obtain ⟨a, s, rfl⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq S x
57:     use a, s, s.2
58:     apply IsLocalization.lift_mk', by
59:     rintro ⟨a, s, hs, rfl⟩
60:     use IsLocalization.mk' _ a ⟨s, hs⟩
61:     apply IsLocalization.lift_mk'⟩
62: 
63: instance isLocalization_range_mapToFractionRing (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
64:     [IsLocalization S B] (hS : S ≤ A⁰) : IsLocalization S (mapToFractionRing K S B hS).range :=
65:   IsLocalization.isLocalization_of_algEquiv S <|
66:     show B ≃ₐ[A] _ from AlgEquiv.ofBijective (mapToFractionRing K S B hS).rangeRestrict (by
67:       refine ⟨fun a b h => ?_, Set.rangeFactorization_surjective⟩
68:       refine (IsLocalization.lift_injective_iff _).2 (fun a b => ?_) (Subtype.ext_iff.1 h)
69:       exact ⟨fun h => congr_arg _ (IsLocalization.injective _ hS h),
70:         fun h => congr_arg _ (IsFractionRing.injective A K h)⟩)
71: 
72: instance isFractionRing_range_mapToFractionRing (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
73:     [IsLocalization S B] (hS : S ≤ A⁰) : IsFractionRing (mapToFractionRing K S B hS).range K :=
74:   IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isLocalization S _ _ hS
75: 
76: /-- Given a commutative ring `A` with fraction ring `K`, and a submonoid `S` of `A` which
77: contains no zero divisor, this is the localization of `A` at `S`, considered as
78: a subalgebra of `K` over `A`.
79: 
80: The carrier of this subalgebra is defined as the set of all `x : K` of the form
81: `IsLocalization.mk' K a ⟨s, _⟩`, where `s ∈ S`.
82: -/
83: noncomputable def subalgebra (hS : S ≤ A⁰) : Subalgebra A K :=
84:   (mapToFractionRing K S (Localization S) hS).range.copy
85:       { x | ∃ (a s : A) (hs : s ∈ S), x = IsLocalization.mk' K a ⟨s, hS hs⟩ } <| by
86:     ext
87:     symm
88:     apply mem_range_mapToFractionRing_iff
89: 
90: namespace subalgebra
91: 
92: instance isLocalization_subalgebra : IsLocalization S (subalgebra K S hS) := by
93:   dsimp +instances only [Localization.subalgebra]
94:   rw [Subalgebra.copy_eq]
95:   infer_instance
96: 
97: instance isFractionRing : IsFractionRing (subalgebra K S hS) K :=
98:   IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isLocalization S _ _ hS
99: 
100: end subalgebra
101: 
102: end CommRing
103: 
104: section Field
105: 
106: variable [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
107: 
108: namespace subalgebra
109: 
110: theorem mem_range_mapToFractionRing_iff_ofField (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
111:     [IsLocalization S B] (x : K) :
112:     x ∈ (mapToFractionRing K S B hS).range ↔
113:       ∃ (a s : A) (_ : s ∈ S), x = algebraMap A K a * (algebraMap A K s)⁻¹ := by
114:   rw [mem_range_mapToFractionRing_iff]
115:   convert! Iff.rfl
116:   congr
117:   rw [Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val]
118:   rfl
119: 
120: /-- Given a domain `A` with fraction field `K`, and a submonoid `S` of `A` which
121: contains no zero divisor, this is the localization of `A` at `S`, considered as
122: a subalgebra of `K` over `A`.
123: 
124: The carrier of this subalgebra is defined as the set of all `x : K` of the form
125: `algebraMap A K a * (algebraMap A K s)⁻¹` where `a s : A` and `s ∈ S`.
126: -/
127: noncomputable def ofField : Subalgebra A K :=
128:   (mapToFractionRing K S (Localization S) hS).range.copy
129:       { x | ∃ (a s : A) (_ : s ∈ S), x = algebraMap A K a * (algebraMap A K s)⁻¹ } <| by
130:     ext
131:     symm
132:     apply mem_range_mapToFractionRing_iff_ofField
133: 
134: theorem ofField_eq : ofField K S hS = subalgebra K S hS := by
135:   simp_rw [ofField, subalgebra, Subalgebra.copy_eq]
136: 
137: instance isLocalization_ofField : IsLocalization S (ofField K S hS) := by
138:   rw [ofField_eq]
139:   exact isLocalization_subalgebra K S hS
140: 
141: instance (S : Subalgebra A K) : IsFractionRing S K := by
142:   refine IsFractionRing.of_field S K fun z ↦ ?_
143:   rcases IsFractionRing.div_surjective A z with ⟨x, y, _, eq⟩
144:   exact ⟨algebraMap A S x, algebraMap A S y, eq.symm⟩
145: 
146: instance isFractionRing_ofField : IsFractionRing (ofField K S hS) K :=
147:   inferInstance
148: 
149: end subalgebra
150: 
151: end Field
152: 
153: end Localization

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.

arguments.header:
import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
def Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ
end SL2Reduction
types: SL2Reduction.R p
SL2Reduction.iota p M
SL2Reduction.qmul p M y v
LinearMap.baseChange K
Module.finrank_pi_fintype
Module.finrank_baseChange

9: 
10: /-!
11: 
12: # The `RestrictScalars` type alias
13: 
14: See the documentation attached to the `RestrictScalars` definition for advice on how and when to
15: use this type alias. As described there, it is often a better choice to use the `IsScalarTower`
16: typeclass instead.
17: 
18: ## Main definitions
19: 
20: * `RestrictScalars R S M`: the `S`-module `M` viewed as an `R` module when `S` is an `R`-algebra.
21:   Note that by default we do *not* have a `Module S (RestrictScalars R S M)` instance
22:   for the original action.
23:   This is available as a def `RestrictScalars.moduleOrig` if really needed.
24: * `RestrictScalars.addEquiv : RestrictScalars R S M ≃+ M`: the additive equivalence
25:   between the restricted and original space (in fact, they are definitionally equal,
26:   but sometimes it is helpful to avoid using this fact, to keep instances from leaking).
27: * `RestrictScalars.ringEquiv : RestrictScalars R S A ≃+* A`: the ring equivalence
28:   between the restricted and original space when the module is an algebra.
29: * `Module.restrictScalars R S M`, `Algebra.restrictScalars R S A`: non-instance definitions for
30:   `Module R M` and `Algebra R A`.
31: 
32: ## See also
33: 
34: There are many similarly-named definitions elsewhere which do not refer to this type alias. These
35: refer to restricting the scalar type in a bundled type, such as from `A →ₗ[R] B` to `A →ₗ[S] B`:
36: 
37: * `LinearMap.restrictScalars`
38: * `LinearEquiv.restrictScalars`
39: * `AlgHom.restrictScalars`
40: * `AlgEquiv.restrictScalars`
41: * `Submodule.restrictScalars`
42: * `Subalgebra.restrictScalars`
43: -/
44: 
45: @[expose] public section
46: 
47: 
48: variable (R S M A : Type*)
49: 
50: /-- If we put an `R`-algebra structure on a semiring `S`, we get a natural equivalence from the
51: category of `S`-modules to the category of representations of the algebra `S` (over `R`). The type
52: synonym `RestrictScalars` is essentially this equivalence.
53: 
54: Warning: use this type synonym judiciously! Consider an example where we want to construct an
55: `R`-linear map from `M` to `S`, given:
56: ```lean
57: variable (R S M : Type*)
58: variable [CommSemiring R] [Semiring S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module S M]
59: ```
60: With the assumptions above we can't directly state our map as we have no `Module R M` structure, but
61: `RestrictScalars` permits it to be written as:
62: ```lean
63: -- an `R`-module structure on `M` is provided by `RestrictScalars` which is compatible
64: example : RestrictScalars R S M →ₗ[R] S := sorry
65: ```
66: However, it is usually better just to add this extra structure as an argument:
67: ```lean
68: -- an `R`-module structure on `M` and proof of its compatibility is provided by the user
69: example [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M] : M →ₗ[R] S := sorry
70: ```
71: The advantage of the second approach is that it defers the duty of providing the missing typeclasses
72: `[Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]`. If some concrete `M` naturally carries these (as is often
73: the case) then we have avoided `RestrictScalars` entirely. If not, we can pass
74: `RestrictScalars R S M` later on instead of `M`.
75: 
76: Note that this means we almost always want to state definitions and lemmas in the language of
77: `IsScalarTower` rather than `RestrictScalars`.
78: 
79: An example of when one might want to use `RestrictScalars` would be if one has a vector space
80: over a field of characteristic zero and wishes to make use of the `ℚ`-algebra structure. -/
81: @[nolint unusedArguments]
82: def RestrictScalars (_R _S M : Type*) : Type _ := M
83: 
84: instance [I : Inhabited M] : Inhabited (RestrictScalars R S M) := I
85: 
86: instance [I : AddCommMonoid M] : AddCommMonoid (RestrictScalars R S M) := I
87: 
88: instance [I : AddCommGroup M] : AddCommGroup (RestrictScalars R S M) := I
89: 
90: section Module
91: 
92: section
93: 
94: variable [Semiring S] [AddCommMonoid M]
95: 
96: /-- We temporarily install an action of the original ring on `RestrictScalars R S M`. -/
97: @[instance_reducible]
98: def RestrictScalars.moduleOrig [I : Module S M] : Module S (RestrictScalars R S M) := I
99: 
100: variable [CommSemiring R] [Algebra R S]
101: 
102: section
103: 
104: attribute [local instance] RestrictScalars.moduleOrig
105: 
106: /-- When `M` is a module over a ring `S`, and `S` is an algebra over `R`, then `M` inherits a
107: module structure over `R`. Not an instance because `S` cannot be inferred.
108: 
109: The preferred way of setting this up is `[Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]`.
110: -/
111: abbrev Module.restrictScalars [Module S M] : Module R M :=
112:   Module.compHom M (algebraMap R S)
113: 
114: /-- When `M` is a module over a ring `S`, and `S` is an algebra over `R`, then `M` inherits a
115: module structure over `R`.
116: 
117: The preferred way of setting this up is `[Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]`.
118: -/
119: instance RestrictScalars.module [Module S M] : Module R (RestrictScalars R S M) :=
120:   Module.restrictScalars R S M
121: 
122: /-- `Module.restrictScalars` forms a scalar tower. -/
123: theorem IsScalarTower.restrictScalars [Module S M] :
124:     letI := Module.restrictScalars R S M
125:     IsScalarTower R S M :=
126:   IsScalarTower.of_compHom R S M
127: 
128: /-- This instance is only relevant when `RestrictScalars.moduleOrig` is available as an instance.
129: -/
130: instance RestrictScalars.isScalarTower [Module S M] : IsScalarTower R S (RestrictScalars R S M) :=
131:   IsScalarTower.restrictScalars R S M
132: 
133: end
134: 
135: /-- When `M` is a right-module over a ring `S`, and `S` is an algebra over `R`, then `M` inherits a
136: right-module structure over `R`.
137: The preferred way of setting this up is
138: `[Module Rᵐᵒᵖ M] [Module Sᵐᵒᵖ M] [IsScalarTower Rᵐᵒᵖ Sᵐᵒᵖ M]`.
139: -/
140: instance RestrictScalars.opModule [Module Sᵐᵒᵖ M] : Module Rᵐᵒᵖ (RestrictScalars R S M) :=
141:   letI : Module Sᵐᵒᵖ (RestrictScalars R S M) := ‹Module Sᵐᵒᵖ M›
142:   Module.compHom M (RingHom.op <| algebraMap R S)
143: 
144: instance RestrictScalars.isCentralScalar [Module S M] [Module Sᵐᵒᵖ M] [IsCentralScalar S M] :
145:     IsCentralScalar R (RestrictScalars R S M) where
146:   op_smul_eq_smul r _x := (op_smul_eq_smul (algebraMap R S r) (_ : M) :)
147: 
148: /-- The `R`-algebra homomorphism from the original coefficient algebra `S` to endomorphisms
149: of `RestrictScalars R S M`.
150: -/
151: def RestrictScalars.lsmul [Module S M] : S →ₐ[R] Module.End R (RestrictScalars R S M) :=
152:   -- We use `RestrictScalars.moduleOrig` in the implementation,
153:   -- but not in the type.
154:   letI : Module S (RestrictScalars R S M) := RestrictScalars.moduleOrig R S M
155:   Algebra.lsmul R R (RestrictScalars R S M)

def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ
end SL2Reduction

42: /-- The `R`-algebra morphism `A → End (M)` corresponding to the representation of the algebra `A`
43: on the `B`-module `M`.
44: 
45: This is a stronger version of `DistribSMul.toLinearMap`, and could also have been
46: called `Algebra.toModuleEnd`.
47: 
48: The typeclasses correspond to the situation where the types act on each other as
49: ```
50: R ----→ B
51: | ⟍     |
52: |   ⟍   |
53: ↓     ↘ ↓
54: A ----→ M
55: ```
56: where the diagram commutes, the action by `R` commutes with everything, and the action by `A` and
57: `B` on `M` commute.
58: 
59: Typically this is most useful with `B = R` as `Algebra.lsmul R R A : A →ₐ[R] Module.End R M`.
60: However this can be used to get the fact that left-multiplication by `A` is right `A`-linear, and
61: vice versa, as
62: ```lean
63: example : A →ₐ[R] Module.End Aᵐᵒᵖ A := Algebra.lsmul R Aᵐᵒᵖ A
64: example : Aᵐᵒᵖ →ₐ[R] Module.End A A := Algebra.lsmul R A A
65: ```
66: respectively; though `LinearMap.mulLeft` and `LinearMap.mulRight` can also be used here.
67: -/
68: def lsmul : A →ₐ[R] Module.End B M where
69:   toFun := DistribSMul.toLinearMap B M
70:   map_one' := LinearMap.ext fun _ => one_smul A _
71:   map_mul' a b := LinearMap.ext <| smul_assoc a b
72:   map_zero' := LinearMap.ext fun _ => zero_smul A _
73:   map_add' _a _b := LinearMap.ext fun _ => add_smul _ _ _
74:   commutes' r := LinearMap.ext <| algebraMap_smul A r
75: 
76: @[simp]
77: theorem lsmul_coe (a : A) : (lsmul R B M a : M → M) = (a • ·) := rfl
78: 
79: lemma lsmul_apply (a : A) (m : M) : lsmul R B M a m = a • m := rfl
80: 
81: lemma lsmul_eq_smul_one (a : A) : lsmul R R M a = a • 1 := rfl
82: 
83: end Algebra

87: section Module
88: 
89: variable [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A]
90: variable [MulAction A M]
91: variable {R} {M}
92: 
93: theorem algebraMap_smul [SMul R M] [IsScalarTower R A M] (r : R) (x : M) :
94:     algebraMap R A r • x = r • x := by
95:   rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, smul_assoc, one_smul]
96: 
97: variable {A} in
98: theorem of_algebraMap_smul [SMul R M] (h : ∀ (r : R) (x : M), algebraMap R A r • x = r • x) :
99:     IsScalarTower R A M where
100:   smul_assoc r a x := by rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul, h]
101: 
102: variable (R M) in
103: theorem of_compHom : letI := MulAction.compHom M (algebraMap R A : R →* A); IsScalarTower R A M :=
104:   letI := MulAction.compHom M (algebraMap R A : R →* A); of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
105: 
106: end Module

108: section Semiring
109: 
110: variable [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
111: variable [Algebra R S] [Algebra S A] [Algebra S B]
112: variable {R S A}
113: 
114: theorem of_algebraMap_eq [Algebra R A]
115:     (h : ∀ x, algebraMap R A x = algebraMap S A (algebraMap R S x)) : IsScalarTower R S A :=
116:   ⟨fun x y z => by simp_rw [Algebra.smul_def, map_mul, mul_assoc, h]⟩

21: ## Main results
22: 
23: * `IsScalarTower.Subalgebra`: if `A/S/R` is a tower and `S₀` is a subalgebra
24:   between `S` and `R`, then `A/S/S₀` is a tower
25: * `IsScalarTower.Subalgebra'`: if `A/S/R` is a tower and `S₀` is a subalgebra
26:   between `S` and `R`, then `A/S₀/R` is a tower
27: * `Subalgebra.restrictScalars`: turn an `S`-subalgebra of `A` into an `R`-subalgebra of `A`,
28:   given that `A/S/R` is a tower

33:   algebraMap := ZMod.castHom h R
34:   smul := fun a r => cast a * r
35:   commutes' := fun a r =>
36:     show (cast a * r : R) = r * cast a by
37:       rcases ZMod.intCast_surjective a with ⟨k, rfl⟩
38:       change ZMod.castHom h R k * r = r * ZMod.castHom h R k
39:       rw [map_intCast, Int.cast_comm]

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
def Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ
end SL2Reduction

SL2Reduction.qmul p M y v

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
def Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance (priority := 50) localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance (priority := 50) localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ

def Preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, f (m : V) ∈ M
def RPreserves (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ localizedImage p M, f u ∈ localizedImage p M
structure LatticeOps (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  x : Module.End ℤ M
  y : Module.End ℤ M
  h : Module.End ℤ M
  X : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  Y : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
def Agrees (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (a : LatticeOps M) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : M, (a.x m : V) = x (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.y m : V) = y (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.h m : V) = h (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.X r m : V) = divided x r (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.Y r m : V) = divided y r (m : V))
def Invariant {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Simple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Invariant W x → Invariant W y → Invariant W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Highest (lam : ℤ) (x h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lam : ℂ) • w
def Admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (c : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (b i : V) = c i) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r)
def extendFamily {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=
  if hi : i < lam.toNat + 1 then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def GeneratorFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Index lam,
    x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
      (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
    y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
    h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def DividedFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
    X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
      ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily lam b (i.val - r)
      else 0) ∧
    Y r (b i) = ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily lam b (i.val + r)
def E (lam : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def MatrixWord {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End F U :=
  ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹) •
    (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))
def BasisLift (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M),
    ∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val
def Principal (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  b ≠ 0 ∧ J p M y v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a ∧
    Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)

end SL2Reduction
open SL2Reduction
types: Target K M x y h
GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h
∀ (hp : CharP K p), letI : CharP K p := hp; letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := ZMod.algebra K p; Nonempty (VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p))

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
def Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance (priority := 50) localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance (priority := 50) localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ

def Preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, f (m : V) ∈ M
def RPreserves (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ localizedImage p M, f u ∈ localizedImage p M
structure LatticeOps (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  x : Module.End ℤ M
  y : Module.End ℤ M
  h : Module.End ℤ M
  X : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  Y : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
def Agrees (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (a : LatticeOps M) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : M, (a.x m : V) = x (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.y m : V) = y (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.h m : V) = h (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.X r m : V) = divided x r (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.Y r m : V) = divided y r (m : V))
def Invariant {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Simple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Invariant W x → Invariant W y → Invariant W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Highest (lam : ℤ) (x h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lam : ℂ) • w
def Admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (c : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (b i : V) = c i) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r)
def extendFamily {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=
  if hi : i < lam.toNat + 1 then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def GeneratorFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Index lam,
    x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
      (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
    y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
    h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def DividedFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
    X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
      ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - r)
      else 0) ∧
    Y r (b i) = ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + r)
def E (lam : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def MatrixWord {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End F U :=
  ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹) •
    (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))
def BasisLift (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M),
    ∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val
def Principal (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  b ≠ 0 ∧ J p M y v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a ∧
    Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)

end SL2Reduction
open SL2Reduction
types: Target K M x y h
GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h

664: finite-dimensional spaces it is the `ι`th basis vector of the dual space.
665: -/
666: @[simps!]
667: def coord : M →ₗ[R] R :=
668:   Finsupp.lapply i ∘ₗ ↑b.repr
669: 
670: theorem forall_coord_eq_zero_iff {x : M} : (∀ i, b.coord i x = 0) ↔ x = 0 :=
671:   Iff.trans (by simp only [b.coord_apply, DFunLike.ext_iff, Finsupp.zero_apply])
672:     b.repr.map_eq_zero_iff
673: 
674: /-- The sum of the coordinates of an element `m : M` with respect to a basis. -/
675: noncomputable def sumCoords : M →ₗ[R] R :=
676:   (Finsupp.lsum ℕ fun _ => LinearMap.id) ∘ₗ (b.repr : M →ₗ[R] ι →₀ R)
677: 
678: @[simp]
679: theorem coe_sumCoords : (b.sumCoords : M → R) = fun m => (b.repr m).sum fun _ => id :=
680:   rfl
681: 
682: @[simp high]
683: theorem coe_sumCoords_of_fintype [Fintype ι] : (b.sumCoords : M → R) = ∑ i, b.coord i := by
684:   ext m

400: 
401: variable [StrongRankCondition R]
402: 
403: /-- The dimension of a submodule is bounded by the dimension of the ambient space. -/
404: theorem Submodule.finrank_le [Module.Finite R M] (s : Submodule R M) :
405:     finrank R s ≤ finrank R M :=
406:   toNat_le_toNat (Submodule.rank_le s) (rank_lt_aleph0 _ _)
407: 
408: /-- Pushforwards of finite submodules have a smaller finrank. -/
409: theorem Submodule.finrank_map_le
410:     [Module R M'] (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (p : Submodule R M) [Module.Finite R p] :
411:     finrank R (p.map f) ≤ finrank R p :=
412:   finrank_le_finrank_of_rank_le_rank (lift_rank_map_le _ _) (rank_lt_aleph0 _ _)
413: 
414: theorem Submodule.finrank_mono {s t : Submodule R M} [Module.Finite R t] (hst : s ≤ t) :
415:     finrank R s ≤ finrank R t :=
416:   Cardinal.toNat_le_toNat (Submodule.rank_mono hst) (rank_lt_aleph0 R ↥t)
417: 
418: end
419: 
420: end SubmoduleRank
421: 
422: section Span
423: 
424: variable [StrongRankCondition R]
425: 
426: theorem rank_span_le (s : Set M) : Module.rank R (span R s) ≤ #s := by
427:   rw [Finsupp.span_eq_range_linearCombination, ← lift_strictMono.le_iff_le]
428:   refine (lift_rank_range_le _).trans ?_
429:   rw [rank_finsupp_self]
430:   simp only [lift_lift, le_refl]
431: 
432: theorem rank_span_finset_le (s : Finset M) : Module.rank R (span R (s : Set M)) ≤ s.card := by
433:   simpa using rank_span_le (s : Set M)
434: 
435: theorem rank_span_of_finset (s : Finset M) : Module.rank R (span R (s : Set M)) < ℵ₀ :=
436:   (rank_span_finset_le s).trans_lt natCast_lt_aleph0

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
def Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance (priority := 50) localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance (priority := 50) localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ

def Preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, f (m : V) ∈ M
def RPreserves (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ localizedImage p M, f u ∈ localizedImage p M
structure LatticeOps (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  x : Module.End ℤ M
  y : Module.End ℤ M
  h : Module.End ℤ M
  X : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  Y : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
def Agrees (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (a : LatticeOps M) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : M, (a.x m : V) = x (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.y m : V) = y (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.h m : V) = h (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.X r m : V) = divided x r (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.Y r m : V) = divided y r (m : V))
def Invariant {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Simple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Invariant W x → Invariant W y → Invariant W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Highest (lam : ℤ) (x h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lam : ℂ) • w
def Admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (c : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (b i : V) = c i) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r)
def extendFamily {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=
  if hi : i < lam.toNat + 1 then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def GeneratorFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Index lam,
    x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
      (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
    y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
    h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def DividedFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
    X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
      ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - r)
      else 0) ∧
    Y r (b i) = ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + r)
def E (lam : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def MatrixWord {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End F U :=
  ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹) •
    (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))
def BasisLift (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M),
    ∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val
def Principal (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  b ≠ 0 ∧ J p M y v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a ∧
    Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)


def Lowering (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℕ,
    h ((y ^ t) v) = (((lam - 2 * (t : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
    x ((y ^ (t + 1)) v) =
      (((((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (lam - (t : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v)
def CoordinateCore (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∃ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, lam.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h
def Coordinates (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ((lam.toNat + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = lam + 1 ∧
  0 < lam.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Index lam) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
  Lowering lam x y h v ∧
  (∀ i : Index lam, e y v i.val ≠ 0) ∧
  CoordinateCore lam x y h v ∧
  DividedFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) (divided x) (divided y)
def LocalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  (iota p M).range = Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V) ∧
  Nonempty (Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (localizedImage p M : Set V) = ⊤ ∧
  (∀ r, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r) ∧
    RPreserves p M (divided x r) ∧ RPreserves p M (divided y r)) ∧
  Preserves M x ∧ Preserves M y ∧ Preserves M h ∧
  RPreserves p M x ∧ RPreserves p M y ∧ RPreserves p M h ∧
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a
def MatrixIdentities (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Index lam,
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    divided x (lam.toNat - i.val) * (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b i (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) * divided y (lam.toNat - j.val) =
      (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℂ) • E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) j ∧
    (∃ c : R p, (c : ℚ) = (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℚ) ∧ IsUnit c) ∧
    E lam b i j = MatrixWord lam (divided x) (divided y) i j ∧
    RPreserves p M (E lam b i j)
def CommonModule (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Index lam, Ji p M y v i.val = J p M y v) ∧
  Nontrivial (J p M y v) ∧ Module.Finite (R p) (J p M y v) ∧
  ∃ c : (Index lam → J p M y v) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M,
    ∀ g, iota p M (c g) = ∑ i : Index lam, (g i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def RationalLine (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (qmul p M y v) ∧
  (qmul p M y v).range = Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v : Set ℂ) ∧
  Module.Finite ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) = 1
def PrincipalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  RationalLine p M y v ∧ (∃ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b) ∧
  ∀ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b → BasisLift p lam M y v b
def TensorMaps (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (hp : CharP K p) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (kap : R p →+* K) : Prop :=
  letI : CharP K p := hp
  letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
  letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
    (psi : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
    (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), psi (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) =
      c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (ModN.mkQ p u)) ∧
    (∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M) (z : VK K M),
      phi (f.baseChange K z) = (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K (phi z)) ∧
    (∀ f : Module.End (R p) (MR p M),
      ∃ fbar : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
        (∀ u, fbar (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f u)) ∧
        ∀ z, psi (f.baseChange K z) = fbar.baseChange K (psi z))
def ScalarReduction (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (hp : CharP K p) (kap : R p →+* K),
    (∀ (r : R p) (a b : ℤ), b ≠ 0 → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b →
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ) → kap r = (a : K) / (b : K)) ∧
    TensorMaps p K hp M kap
def ReducedBasis (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
  ∃ (beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M)) (b : ℂ),
    Principal p M y v b ∧
    (∃ (kap : R p →+* K),
      letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
      ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
        (c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)),
        (∀ (s : K) (m : M), phi (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
        (∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val) ∧
        ∀ i, phi (beta i) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R p] (c i)) ∧
    Module.finrank K (VK K M) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
    GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)
def ReducedUnits (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  (∀ j : Index lam, (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
    (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat →
      (a.X r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.x.baseChange K) ^ r ∧
      (a.Y r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.y.baseChange K) ^ r) ∧
    ∃ beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M),
      GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K) ∧
      ∀ i j k : Index lam,
        MatrixWord lam (fun r => (a.X r).baseChange K) (fun r => (a.Y r).baseChange K) i j (beta k) =
          if j = k then beta i else 0

end SL2Reduction
open SL2Reduction
